newsitem.title: MEXICO: Six police killed in Mexican guerrilla attacks.
newsitem.headline: Six police killed in Mexican guerrilla attacks.

text.p: Marxist rebels attacked police in two Mexican states on Thursday and Friday, killing six officers and wounding several others less than a week after a ceasefire expired, authorities said.

Newspapers said the attacks were the latest in a wave of hostilities against the security forces by the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), which was calling on Mexicans to rise up against President Ernesto Zedillo's government.

Five officers died when guerrillas, thought to be from the EPR, ambushed a police patrol near the tourist city of Oaxaca, about 220 miles (360 km) southeast of Mexico City on Thursday night, state officials said. Two other policemen were wounded.

On Thursday morning, a police officer died and two were injured in the State of Mexico when four men wearing military-style uniforms fired a hail of bullets and threw molotov cocktails at the local police station of Coacalco, just outside Mexico City.

In a third attack in Guerrero state on Wednesday night, armed rebels opened fire close to a police academy in the town of Atoyac, 50 miles (80 km) west of the resort of Acapulco. No one was killed or injured in the attack, newspapers said.

The EPR did not immediately claim responsibility for the attacks in Guerrero and Oaxaca, but did take credit for the attack near Mexico City in a statement sent to La Jornada newspaper, the daily reported on Friday.
If it was the work of the shadowy rebel group, the attacks would mark the EPR's biggest operations since its month-long unilateral ceasefire, which expired on Oct. 27.
Police in Coacalco said at least two men pulled up to the station on Thursday in an expensive car with U.S. license plates and opened fire using AK-47 automatic rifles.
"They suddenly started shooting and we began to shoot back. We injured one of them," an unidentified policeman at the station told the Televisa TV network.
Officials said they believed the EPR was behind the attacks. Pro-EPR slogans were spray-painted at one scene, said state spokesman Gabino Cue Monteagudo.

Little is known about the size or strength of the EPR, a left-wing rebel group that first appeared in Mexico in June vowing to overthrow the government. Mexico's army has since launched massive sweeps in several states in search of the elusive rebels.

The attacks came a day after the top Mexican naval commander in Oaxaca told reporters the rebel group had been rendered incapable of carrying out new attacks in the state because security forces had arrested all its top people.
